'''Leonid Kostyantynovych Kadenyuk''' ({{langx|uk|Леонід Костянтинович Каденюк}}; 28 January 1951&nbsp;– 31 January 2018)<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 January 2018 |title=Помер космонавт Леонід Каденюк |trans-title=Cosmonaut Leonid Kadenyuk died |url=https://www.bbc.com/ukrainian/news-42884403 |accessdate=2 December 2020 |work=BBC News Ukraine |language=uk}}</ref> was the first [[astronaut]] of independent [[Ukraine]] to fly into outer space. 

In 1997, he flew on [[NASA]]'s [[Space Shuttle Columbia|Space Shuttle ''Columbia'']] as part of the international mission [[STS-87]].<ref name="MPC-object" /><ref name="babel">{{cite web |url=https://babel.ua/en/texts/54853-26-years-ago-leonid-kadeniuk-became-the-first-and-currently-the-only-astronaut-of-independent-ukraine-this-is-how-he-increased-the-prestige-of-the-country-as-a-space-state-here-is-his-story-in-archiva |title=26 years ago, Leonid Kadeniuk became the first (and currently the only) astronaut of independent Ukraine. This is how he increased the prestige of the country as a space state. |first=Serhii |last=Pyvovarov |editor-first=Yevhen |editor-last=Spirin
 |date=20 November 2023 |work=Babel |department=Stories |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118092234/https://babel.ua/en/texts/54853-26-years-ago-leonid-kadeniuk-became-the-first-and-currently-the-only-astronaut-of-independent-ukraine-this-is-how-he-increased-the-prestige-of-the-country-as-a-space-state-here-is-his-story-in-archiva |archive-date=18 November 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=26 January 2026}}</ref>

Kadenyuk held the rank of [[major general]] in the [[Ukrainian Air Force]]. He was Deputy of Ukraine of the 4th convocation, adviser to the [[Prime Minister of Ukraine]], Chairman of the [[State Space Agency of Ukraine]], and [[Honorary degree|Honorary Doctor]] of [[Chernivtsi University|Chernivtsi National University.]]

From 2015 until his death, he served as president of the Aerospace Society of Ukraine.

Designated a [[Hero of Ukraine]] in December 1999,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-22 |title=Про нагородження відзнакою П... {{!}} від 03.12.1999 № 1526/99 |url=https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/cgi-bin/laws/main.cgi?nreg=1526/99 |access-date=2024-11-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190522084223/https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/cgi-bin/laws/main.cgi?nreg=1526/99 |archive-date=22 May 2019 }}</ref> he is the namesake of the [[Chernivtsi International Airport|Chernivtsi Leonid Kadenyuk International Airport]].

== Life ==

=== Early life and education ===
Leonid Kadenyuk was born on 28 January 1951 in the village of [[Klishkivtsi]] in the [[Khotyn Raion]] of the [[Chernivtsi Oblast]] in Ukraine, to a family of rural teachers.

In 1967, he graduated from high school with a silver medal, after which he entered the [[Chernihiv Air Base|Chernihiv Higher Military Aviation School of Pilots]].

After graduating from the Aviation School in 1971 and receiving a diploma as a pilot-engineer specializing in aircraft pilotry/operations, he worked as a pilot-instructor.

=== USSR pilotry and military service ===
Kadenyuk was a Soviet military pilot. He began his service in the [[Soviet Air Forces]] and was selected in 1976 for the [[List of astronauts by year of selection#1976|Soviet Cosmonaut Corps]]. In 1977 he graduated from the Test Pilot Training Center. He received a diploma and qualification "[[test pilot]]". In 1977–1979, he underwent general space training and qualified as a test astronaut.

Between 1984 and 1988 Kadenyuk was a [[test pilot]] of the State Research Institute of the [[Soviet Union|USSR]] [[Soviet Air Forces|Air Force]]. In 1989 he graduated from the [[Moscow Aviation Institute]] – Faculty of Aircraft. Between 1988 and 1990 he underwent engineering and flight training in the [[Buran program|''Buran'' program]] as commander of the planned Soviet reusable spacecraft.{{citation needed|date=February 2023}} He was removed from a team of test pilots of [[Buran (spacecraft)|''Buran'']] due to marital issues. He was allowed to rejoin the Cosmonaut Detachment several years later.<ref>{{cite book |title=World Manned Cosmonautics – History, Equipment, People (Russian language) |date=2005 |publisher=Moscow Publishing House |editor=Baturin |editor-first=Yuri M. |pages=600–601}}</ref> He took part in working out the [[Glider (aircraft)|glide]] path of descent for landing the spacecraft ''Buran'' using [[Mikoyan MiG-31|MiG-31]] and [[Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25|MiG-25]] aircraft.

Between 1990 and 1992, under the full program, he was trained as the commander of the transport ship [[Soyuz-TM]].

=== Post-Ukrainian independence ===
With the [[History of the Soviet Union (1982–91)|break-up of the Soviet Union]], Kadenyuk remained in the [[Russian Space Forces]] and adopted Ukrainian [[citizenship]].<ref name="Люди" /> In 1995, during the preparation of the first Ukrainian space mission, he volunteered to take part and returned to his homeland.<ref name="Люди">{{Cite web |last=peoples.ru |title=Биография Леонид Каденюк |trans-title=Biography Leonid Kadenyuk |url=https://www.peoples.ru/military/cosmos/kadenuk/index.html |access-date= |website=www.peoples.ru |language=ru}}</ref>

In 1995 he was selected to the group of astronauts of the [[State Space Agency of Ukraine|National Space Agency of Ukraine]].

Preparing for space flight, from April to October 1996 he worked as a researcher at the Department of Phytohormonology of the Kholodny Institute of Botany of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].

=== 1997 flight with Space Shuttle ''Columbia'' ===
{{Main|STS-87}}
[[File:STS-87_traditional_in-flight_crew_portrait.jpg|right|thumb|190x190px|[[STS-87]]'s in-flight crew portrait, including [[Steven Lindsey|Steven W. Lindsey]]; [[Takao Doi]]; [[Winston E. Scott]]; [[Kevin R. Kregel]]; [[Kalpana Chawla]]; and Kadenyuk.]]
He was trained by [[NASA]] for a space flight on [[Space Shuttle Columbia|Space Shuttle ''Columbia'']]'s mission [[STS-87]] as a payload specialist. There were two main candidates for the mission, the other being [[Yaroslav Pustovyi]], a civil Ukrainian scientist in space research. As the more experienced one, Kadenyuk was chosen as the primary candidate for the mission, and Pustovy became Kadenyuk's backup.

During the preparation for space flights and in the process of test work he underwent unique engineering and flight training. He studied the [[Soyuz (spacecraft)|Soyuz]], [[Soyuz-TM]], [[Buran (spacecraft)|Buran spacecraft]], the Salyut orbital station, the Mir orbital complex, and the [[Space Shuttle|US Space Shuttle]]. He was trained to conduct scientific experiments on board spacecraft in various fields: biology, medicine, metrology, ecology, study of natural resources of the Earth from space, geology, astronomy, geobotany.

From 19 November to 5 December 1997, he made a space flight on the American Space Shuttle ''Columbia'', mission STS-87. The 24th flight of Columbia took place with the participation of Leonid Kadenyuk on 19 November 1997, launched from the [[Kennedy Space Center]]. In the laboratory module "Spacelab" scientific experiments in the fields of astrobiology, physics and materials science were carried out, astronauts were also scheduled to go into outer space.
[[File:STS087-362-020 - STS-087 - CUE - BPAC, Kadenyuk holds up PGCs - DPLA - 131645a776ec8d0a8549ea8decb24beb.jpg|thumb|Kadenyuk holds up a ''[[Brassica rapa]]'' plant growth experiment while aboard the ''[[Space Shuttle Columbia|Columbia]]'', January 1998 ]]
During his flight with shuttle Columbia, he performed biological experiments of a joint Ukrainian-American scientific study with three species of plants: turnip, soybean and moss. The main purpose of the experiments was to study the effect of weightlessness on the photosynthetic apparatus of plants, on fertilization and embryo development, on gene expression in soybean and turnip tissues, on the content of phytohormones in turnip plants, on hydrocarbon metabolism and ultrastructure of soybean sprout cells. 

In addition to these experiments in space flight, experiments were performed by the Institute of Systems Human Research on the topic "Man and the state of weightlessness."

On 27 November, the 9th day of the flight, the first connection with Ukraine was scheduled. For the first time from space, a citizen of Ukraine had a dialogue with his country.

From the astronaut's memoirs: "7 days before the launch, a special regime was introduced for our crew in order to prevent infectious diseases – quarantine. It excludes the possibility of astronauts in public places and any outside contacts. We were also isolated from families. At the same time, the astronauts are not only under the close supervision of doctors, but also under the supervision of psychologists."
[[File:STS087-329-032 - STS-087 - Candid views of crewmember activity in the middeck - DPLA - 240623c0d0792b3af246c719c1922035.jpg|thumb|Candid photograph in middeck with American pilot [[Steven Lindsey|Steve Lindsey]], January 1998]]
Leonid Kostyantynovych recalls: "Every free minute I and my colleagues used to observe and photograph the Earth and space. Such classes were the most popular, and I considered them another impressive and extremely interesting experiment aboard the "Columbia"".

The day in Ukraine begins with the Anthem. Therefore, Leonid Kostyantynovych ordered it to signal the awakening of the crew, which was broadcast from the Flight Control Center on board the "Columbia". Each member of the crew chose a melody to their liking. Thus, the anthem of our state twice sounded in space over the entire planet.

=== Later pilot career ===
After the flight, Leonid Kadenyuk continued his [[:Category:Space program of Ukraine|Ukrainian space program]] career at the [[State Space Agency of Ukraine]].

He participated in the development and testing of aerospace systems, in their sketch and layout design, as well as in-flight tests of systems.

He flew more than 50 types and modifications of aircraft for various purposes, mainly on fighters, as well as on the [[Trainer aircraft|American training aircraft]] [[Northrop T-38 Talon|Northrop T-38]].

Kadenyuk was appointed [[Major general]] of the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine]] in 1998 and became Deputy Inspector General of the General Military Inspectorate under the [[President of Ukraine]] for Aviation and Cosmonautics.

=== Political career ===
In the [[2002 Ukrainian parliamentary election|2002 parliamentary election]], he was elected to the [[Verkhovna Rada]] in the list of pro-[[Leonid Kuchma|Kuchma]] [[For United Ukraine!|United Ukraine Bloc]]. Later, Kadenyuk joined the "[[Labour Ukraine|Trudova Ukrayina – Industrialists and Entrepreneurs]]" faction, but had not been politically active. He worked within parliament's Committee on Defense and National Security.

In the [[2006 Ukrainian parliamentary election|2006 parliamentary election]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://w1.c1.rada.gov.ua/pls/site2/p_deputat_list?skl=5|title=Народні депутати України IV скликання (2002–2006)|date=5 February 2018}}</ref> Kadenyuk was No. 3 in the electoral party list of [[Lytvyn Bloc|Lytvyn's People's Bloc]], but the block won only 2.44% of the popular vote (short of the required 3%) and no seats in the parliament.

=== Writings ===
Kadenyuk is the author of 5 scientific papers. The book "Mission – Space", published in 2009 by Pulsary Publishing House, won first place in the Book of the Year 2009 competition in the Horizons category. The book was republished in 2017 by Novy Druk Publishing House.
== Awards and honors ==

Award of the President of Ukraine "[[Hero of Ukraine]]" with the award of the Order "Golden Star" – for services to the Ukrainian state in the development of astronautics, outstanding personal contribution to strengthening international cooperation in space.

On 19 January 1998, Kadenyuk received the [[Order for Courage|Order "For Courage"]] I degree of the Distinction of the President of Ukraine for outstanding contribution to the international prestige of the national space industry and personal courage and heroism shown during the Ukrainian-American scientific research aboard the [[Space Shuttle Columbia]].

Order "For Merits" III st. – for significant personal contribution to the development of the rocket and space industry, significant achievements in the creation and implementation of space systems and technologies, high professionalism (12 April 2011)[[File:Тальський Р.Б., Каденюк Л.К..jpg|thumb|Politician {{Interlanguage link|Rostyslav Talsky|uk|Тальський Ростислав Борисович}} of the [[Kyiv]] {{Interlanguage link|Bukovina Society|uk|Буковинське земляцтво}} congratulating Kadenyuk as a Hero of Ukraine, 2009]]In 2004, astronomers at [[Andrushivka Astronomical Observatory]] named Asteroid [[399673 Kadenyuk]] in his honor.<ref name="MPC-object" /> The official {{MoMP|399673|naming citation}} was published by the [[Minor Planet Center]] on 5 October 2017 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 106504}}).<ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" />

== Death and legacy ==

Kadenyuk died on 31 January 2018 from a [[heart attack]] during his morning run in a park in [[Kyiv]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Pearlman |first=Robert Z. |title=Leonid Kadenyuk, First Ukrainian Astronaut Who Flew on US Space Shuttle, Dies at 67 |url=https://www.space.com/39693-ukranian-astronaut-leonid-kadenyuk-obituary.html |work=[[Space.com]] |date=14 February 2018 |access-date=26 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913211751/https://www.space.com/39693-ukranian-astronaut-leonid-kadenyuk-obituary.html |archive-date=13 September 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Melkozerova |first=Veronika |work=[[Kyiv Post]] |date=31 January 2018 |title=Ukraine's first astronaut Leonid Kadenyuk dies at 67 |url=https://www.kyivpost.com/post/10231 |access-date=26 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821105407/https://www.kyivpost.com/post/10231 |archive-date=21 August 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was interred in the central avenue of [[Kyiv]]'s [[Baikove Cemetery]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 July 2018 |title=На Байковому цвинтарі попрощалися з дисидентом Левком Лук'яненком (відео) |trans-title=They said goodbye to the dissident Levko Lukyanenko at Baikovo cemetery (video) |url=https://www.unian.ua/society/10182767-na-baykovomu-cvintari-poproshchalisya-z-disidentom-levkom-luk-yanenkom-video.html |access-date= |website=[[Ukrainian Independent Information Agency]] |language=uk}}</ref> 

On 2 February 2018, the farewell ceremony occurred in Kyiv in the Club of [[Government of Ukraine|Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine]] building.<ref>{{Cite web |title=У Києві попрощалися з першим космонавтом незалежної України Леонідом Каденюком – Новини – Перший канал |trans-title=In Kyiv, they said goodbye to the first cosmonaut of independent Ukraine, Leonid Kadenyuk - News - Channel One |url=https://tv.suspilne.media/news/99446 |access-date=22 October 2020 |website=tv.suspilne.media |language=uk}}</ref> 

In September of the same year, the [[Chernivtsi International Airport|Chernivtsi Leonid Kadenyuk International Airport]] was named for Kadenyuk.<ref>{{cite web |date=28 September 2018 |title=Airport in Chernivtsi named after Ukrainian spaceman Kadeniuk |work=Kyiv Post |agency=[[Interfax-Ukraine]] |url=https://archive.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/airport-in-chernivtsi-named-after-ukrainian-spaceman-kadeniuk.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125062835/https://archive.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/airport-in-chernivtsi-named-after-ukrainian-spaceman-kadeniuk.html |archive-date=25 January 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 April 2020, sculptor [[Valentyn Znoba]] created a [[Relief|bas-relief]] portrait of Kadenyuk for the [[Kyiv Polytechnic Institute|National Technical University of Ukraine]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=In Memory of the First Astronaut of Independent Ukraine |first=Serhii |last=Hrachov |date=28 January 2021 |work=[[Kyiv Polytechnic Institute]] |department=Department of History of Aviation and Cosmonautics |url=https://kpi.ua/en/kadeniuk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113211039/https://kpi.ua/en/kadeniuk |archive-date=13 November 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=26 January 2026}}</ref> The bust has been treated as a memorial, as staff and students leave flowers there on 28 January, Kadenyuk's birthday.<ref name=":0" /><gallery mode="packed" widths="200" perrow="1">
File:Stamp of Ukraine s813 (cropped).jpg|2007 Ukrainian postage stamp reading "L. Kadenyuk - the first cosmonaut of Ukraine".
File:Пам'ятник Леоніду Каденюку на Байковому кладовищі.jpeg|2020 monument to Kadenyuk at [[Baikove Cemetery]]. It was unveiled on 5 December, the 23rd anniversary of his return from [[STS-87]].
File:Leonid Kadenyuk Room in Air and Space Museum in Chernivtsi.jpg|A room dedicated to Kadenyuk in the [[Chernivtsi Air and Space Museum]]
</gallery>
